subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler TCO — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler TCO — post-call recap & next steps

Alex — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Call highlights (from our side):
- FinPay primary goal: move AI assistants in product to a predictable, cost-efficient inference stack with <100ms token tail latency for short-turn prompts.
- Main competitors you mentioned: Hyperscaler vendor-managed endpoints (H-API), and CompetitorX inference API.
- Key evaluation criteria: per-1M token cost, latency at target qps, cold vs warmed KV cache behavior, batching impact, and security controls for PCI/PII.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) We will share a per-1M token TCO spreadsheet with assumptions for hosted Redwood + Dedicated (reserved) vs H-API and CompetitorX — see attached (redwood_vs_hyperscaler_tco_sheet.xlsx).
2) Proposed tests: Marcus will run a Dedicated quantized run with batching 8/16 and KV cache enabled on a small 10k-prompt sample you provide; we’ll capture tokens-per-second, 95th latency, and effective cost per-1M tokens under varying cache hit rates.
3) We need a ~1k representative prompt sample (anonymized) and a short traffic profile (qps, avg prompt length) to mirror production. If you prefer, upload to the Drive link you mentioned or send as attachment.
4) We'll document assumptions (model family, input length, output length, quantization) — please flag any preference for model family (e.g., LLaMA-derivative vs GPT-like).

Numbers and assumptions will be in the sheet, but high-level ballpark from today: Redwood hosted (non-dedicated) typically shows 15-30% lower per-token unit cost vs H-API for our comparator models when batching & caching are enabled; Dedicated reserved capacity drives another 20-40% reduction depending on commit level and cache hit. We’ll put exact per-1M token lines in the sheet.

Please confirm: 1) you can share the sample prompt set; 2) target latency SLO (is 100ms tail still the goal?); and 3) whether you want us to simulate your burst profile (we can).

Thanks — I’ll loop Marcus and Marissa for test ownership.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_tco_sheet.xlsx

From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@finpay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler TCO — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers and follow-ups from our side: 

- We can share a 1k anonymized prompt sample. I'll upload to the Drive folder by tomorrow EOD. The sample will include both short prompts (avg 30 tokens) and a smaller slice of long form (avg 250 tokens).
- 100ms tail is the target for short prompts, 200ms acceptable for longer generator prompts.
- On batching: our current infra uses batching up to 16 for async workloads; for interactive UI we keep batch sizes small (~4-8). Please capture both 8 and 16.
- Cache hit expectations: realistic steady-state hit ~40-60% (we have prefix reuse in a lot of flows), but cold-start scenarios matter for user-facing paths. For the test, please run 30% and 60% cache hit sims.

A couple specifics we'd like to see in the TCO lines: 
1) Per-1M tokens cost breakdowns (model compute, infra amortization, network) for Redwood hosted, Redwood Dedicated (40% commit example), H-API, and CompetitorX.
2) Cost sensitivity if average output length is +50% vs baseline.
3) Latency at P95/P99 for your recommended configs.

We'll also want to validate that any dedicated option can be configured to failover to hosted or another region in case of capacity constraints. Can you include a note on fallbacks?

One more ask: can Marcus/your infra team run the Dedicated quantized run on a similar GPU profile to what H-API uses for parity (NVIDIA A10x or equivalent)? That will help make the comparison apples-to-apples.

Alex
Head of ML Platforms | FinPay
alex.jones@finpay.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler TCO — post-call recap & next steps

Alex — perfect, thanks for the clarifications. Attached is the working TCO sheet (same as in Drive) and a short assumptions tab. Key numbers pulled out here for quick reference (all numbers are illustrative until we run the dedicated test):

Assumptions (baseline): model: Llama-35B-Base-like, avg input 40 tokens, avg output 60 tokens, quantization: 8-bit dynamic, batch 8/16, HW: NVIDIA A10x-equivalent

Ballpark per-1M tokens (USD) — baseline (no cache)
- Redwood Hosted (shared): $48 per 1M tokens
- Redwood Dedicated (40% commit): $32 per 1M tokens
- Hyperscaler H-API (managed endpoints): $60 per 1M tokens
- CompetitorX API: $55 per 1M tokens

Impact of caching (effective cost with cache hits):
- At 30% cache hit: Dedicated -> ~$25 per 1M (effective), Hosted -> ~$38 per 1M
- At 60% cache hit: Dedicated -> ~$18 per 1M, Hosted -> ~$28 per 1M

Batching sensitivity (relative to per-token cost):
- Batch 8: baseline as above
- Batch 16: reduces compute overhead ~10-15% on our runtime for these models (depends on seq lengths)

Latency (approx P95) on A10x-equivalent:
- Batch 4: ~70-110ms (short prompts)
- Batch 8: ~85-140ms
- Batch 16: ~120-200ms (higher tail for interactive)

Notes: 
- Dedicated assumes reserved pool sized for your qps with KV cache warmed on steady-state traffic. Cost numbers include infra amortization + runtime ops but exclude network egress for simplicity — sheet contains full breakout.
- Failover: Redwood Dedicated can be configured with automated fallback policies to route to compatible hosted variants or alternate regions; we’ll outline the policy options in the doc.

Next steps we propose: 
- Marcus to run Dedicated quantized tests on A10x-equivalent with: batch sizes [8,16], cache hit sims [30%,60%], 1k prompt sample (you’ll upload). Capture tokens/sec, P95/P99 latency, and per-1M effective cost.
- FinPay: upload prompt sample to the Drive link and confirm any redaction rules.
- We’ll reconcile sheet numbers and deliver final TCO + test artifacts (logs, charts) within 5 business days of receiving the sample.

Marcus — can you confirm you have access to an A10x-equivalent instance and can schedule the run once Alex uploads the sample? I attached the run configuration (look under the "Test Plan" tab in the sheet).

Thanks — I’ll update the HubSpot deal with these next steps (link included).

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_tco_sheet.xlsx, finpay_sample_workload.json

Thanks — confirming I can run the Dedicated quantized tests on an A10x-equivalent host. Plan:
- Schedule runs tomorrow morning (2 hours) with configs: batch=8 & batch=16, cache sim scripts for 30% and 60% hits, quantization=8-bit dynamic, sample size=1k prompts.
- Output: raw logs, tokens/sec, P95/P99 latency, and automated per-1M cost calc. I’ll push results and graphs to the Drive folder and update the HubSpot record when done.

Alex — once you upload the sample to the Drive link, please add a short note on redaction (PII removal) so our engineers can skip any sensitive fields. If you prefer to share via SFTP, PM me and we’ll coordinate.
